sources_considered.why: Uber COO on not being able to link token spend to output; budget exhausted in four months.
WIRED summary: 8x8 estimates Claude-driven savings above its Claude bill; a possible counterexample.
Generic survey commentary; does not identify specific large spenders.

receipt.public_excerpt: “If you’re not actually able to draw a direct line to how [many] useful features and functionality you’re shipping to your users, that trade becomes harder to justify,” Macdonald said.

evidence_items.explanation: A large token spender's executive says he cannot link the spending to output. This fits the claim but is one company.

receipt.public_excerpt: the firm had already burnt through its entire 2026 AI coding tools budget in just four months

evidence_items.explanation: Uber did not forecast its token costs well. This fits the 'hard to predict cost' reading for one firm.

receipt.public_excerpt: the company estimates it has saved about $5 million in annual costs by canceling subscriptions to dozens of software and educational tools

evidence_items.explanation: A company claims a measured saving above its Claude bill. But the bill is only 'well below' $5M, so it may not be a 'millions on tokens' spender. The report is also after the post and self-reported, so it is not decisive.

unresolved_gaps: Found no company that clearly spends millions on tokens and publicly reports a specific, measured return above that spend before the post.
Sweeping 'everybody/nobody' claims cannot be confirmed by a few examples; Uber is one firm.
Whether self-reported savings count as 'really knowing' ROI is a matter of judgment.
